title: Directed unions of ideal modules are colimits
statement: Let X be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], I an ideal sheaf [def-nagata-extended-ideal], and S a nonempty set of ideal sheaves directed by inclusion with sSup S = I. Let D : S → Mod(O_X) be a diagram with a cocone τ into I.toModules [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Suppose each stage is identified by e_a : D(a) ≅ a.toModules, and e_a.inv followed by τ_a and the inclusion of I into O_X equals the inclusion of a into O_X. Then the displayed cocone is a colimit.

source.place: Properties of Schemes, Lemma 28.23.3, Tag 01PG; Sheaves of Modules, Definition 17.9.1, Tag 01B4

proof.text: The compatibility equation and the stage isomorphism imply that τ_a is injective on every open. On an affine U, ideal_iSup and the directed-supremum membership lemma identify each section of I with the image of a section of some D(a). These are Mathlib lattice identities plus range_toModulesι_app.

For another cocone s, map an affine section through a chosen stage lift and then through s_a. Compare two lifts in a common upper stage: naturality of τ and its sectionwise injectivity identify them, and naturality of s identifies their images. Comparing sums in a common upper stage and scalar multiples in the same stage proves linearity. Naturality proves compatibility with restrictions.

Apply TopCat.Sheaf.restrictHomEquivHom on the affine basis to extend the additive maps. Check scalar linearity on the same basis using eq_of_locally_eq', so the extension is a module morphism. The basis hom_ext theorem proves the cocone factorization and its uniqueness. IsColimit.ofExistsUnique supplies the colimit proof.

proof_origin.place: Expanded the affine generator and union arguments of Tags 01PG and 01B4 into complete Lean proofs.

mathlib_searches.query: A sheaf of ideals whose sections on affine opens are finitely generated is a finite type sheaf of modules
A finite type ideal sheaf is a finite type sheaf of modules and a directed union of ideal sheaves is their colimit
mathlib_searches.results: Found IdealSheafData.ofIdeals, ideal_sSup, ideal_iSup and SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType. None states either bridge for IdealSheafData.toModules.
Found IsFiniteType, its constructor and local generator projection, and the finite-presentation instance. Finite-type ideals need not be finitely presented.

The source library has toModulesOfLE and its inclusion identity in Curve.DivisorIdealSheaf. Mathlib has directed supremum membership and affine basis morphism extension, but no ideal-module bridge theorem.

lean.statement:
theorem nonempty_isColimit_of_directed_ideal_modules {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) (S : Set X.IdealSheafData)
    (hne : S.Nonempty) (hdir : DirectedOn (· ≤ ·) S) (hunion : sSup S = I)
    (D : S ⥤ X.Modules) (τ : D ⟶ (Functor.const S).obj I.toModules)
    (e : ∀ a : S, D.obj a ≅ a.val.toModules)
    (he : ∀ a : S, (e a).inv ≫ τ.app a ≫ I.toModulesι = a.val.toModulesι) :
    Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk I.toModules τ))
